CausalChain: Chronic liver injury/viral infection/alcohol exposure -> Induction of oxidative stress and hypoxia -> Upregulation of hypoxia-responsive lncRNAs -> m6A methyltransferases modify and stabilize these lncRNAs -> Stabilized lncRNAs enhance HIF-1α signaling and promote glycolytic reprogramming -> Activation of CSC-associated pathways -> Enhanced proliferation and metastasis of HCC
Hypothesis: m6A modifications on hypoxia-responsive lncRNAs function as a critical switch linking oxidative stress to metabolic reprogramming and CSC maintenance in HCC; targeting this m6A-mediated stabilization may suppress HIF-1α-driven metabolic shifts and reduce HCC progression.
Abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is characterized by a hypoxic and oxidative liver microenvironment that drives metabolic reprogramming and supports cancer stem cell (CSC) maintenance. We propose that N6‐methyladenosine (m6A) modifications on hypoxia‐responsive long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs) serve as a molecular switch that integrates redox stress signals with the activation of metabolic and stem cell pathways in HCC. Specifically, under hypoxic conditions, enhanced m6A modification stabilizes lncRNAs such as linc‐RoR, thereby potentiating HIF-1α signaling, promoting a glycolytic phenotype, and sustaining CSC properties. This novel mechanism may contribute to HCC progression and offers a potential therapeutic target by disrupting the lncRNA-m6A regulatory module.
